import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('/data/nls_bmi_processed.csv')
df.head()

# Filter the data to include only Hispanic men
hispanic_men = df[(df['GENDER'] == 'MALE') & (df['HISPANIC'] == 1)]

# Display the first few rows of the filtered data
hispanic_men.head()

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Correlation analysis between BMI and DISSAVED, SAMESAVE
correlation_dissaved = hispanic_men['BMI'].corr(hispanic_men['DISSAVED'])
correlation_samesave = hispanic_men['BMI'].corr(hispanic_men['SAMESAVE'])

print(f"Correlation between BMI and DISSAVED: {correlation_dissaved}")
print(f"Correlation between BMI and SAMESAVE: {correlation_samesave}")

# Scatter plots to visualize the relationship
sns.scatterplot(x='DISSAVED', y='BMI', data=hispanic_men)
plt.title('BMI vs DISSAVED')
plt.show()

sns.scatterplot(x='SAMESAVE', y='BMI', data=hispanic_men)
plt.title('BMI vs SAMESAVE')
plt.show()

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# Prepare the data for regression
X = hispanic_men[['DISSAVED', 'SAMESAVE']].values
y = hispanic_men['BMI'].values
